title: Episode 2 (lines 740–1091)

teacherSummary.text: Creon arrives with smooth words. When Oedipus refuses him, Creon reveals that his men have seized Ismene and drags off Antigone. Theseus arrives, rebukes Creon for breaking Athenian law, and sends men to rescue the girls. Creon calls Oedipus polluted; Oedipus answers that he acted unknowingly.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Howbeit, I know I waste my words—begone, / And leave me here; whate’er may be my lot, / He lives not ill who lives withal content.” slowly and put it in my own words: Oedipus tells Creon that talking is useless: go, and leave him here; whatever happens, a man who is content does not live badly. Next, craft. I notice a sharp dismissal ends in a calm saying about contentment. The strongest word is “content”: satisfied with one's lot. Then, effect. What does Oedipus' claim that a contented man does not live ill reveal about how he has changed? My answer: The claim that a contented man does not live ill reveals how Oedipus has changed: the king who once demanded every answer now asks nothing of Creon except to be left in the place he has chosen.
